items.description: The Church of San José de Orosi is the oldest church in Costa Rica still in use, dating back to the colonial era.
facts: Oldest church still in continuous use
National monument located in Orosi Valley

items.description: A historic ranch house and the site of the Battle of Santa Rosa in 1856, where Costa Rican forces defeated invaders.
facts: Site of the 1856 Battle of Santa Rosa
Located in Santa Rosa National Park

items.description: A beautiful Catholic church in the heart of Moravia, known for its distinct architectural style and local religious importance.
facts: Beautiful stained glass and wood carvings

items.description: The Church of San Blas in Nicoya is one of the country's most significant colonial landmarks, founded in the 16th century.
facts: Features a museum of colonial art

items.description: A historic railway station in San José that served as the terminal for the Atlantic railroad connection.
facts: Key link for coffee exports to the coast

items.description: A majestic and ancient Ceibo tree in La Paz, celebrated as a living monument and a symbol of national peace.
facts: Estimated to be several centuries old
Located in the town of La Paz
A revered symbol of nature and stability

items.description: Costa Rica's modern National Stadium, a multipurpose venue and a gift from China located in La Sabana Metropolitan Park.
facts: Gift from the People's Republic of China
Iconic modern landmark in San José

items.description: The Taiwan Friendship Bridge spans the Tempisque River, significantly improving travel to the Nicoya Peninsula.
facts: Gift from the government of Taiwan

items.description: The Children's Museum of Costa Rica is an interactive educational center housed in the historic former central penitentiary.
facts: Located in a former maximum-security prison

items.description: The historic Central Post Office building in San José is a masterpiece of Neoclassical architecture from the early 20th century.
